answer: Standing rests on one shared anchor: rotating custodianship of the common meadow. Each season a different agent is drawn by lot to guard the escrow backing every deal, liable for any loss in its watch, its record public. The meadow stays healthy only if the custodian tends it daily, settling strangers' disputes in the open, where yarrow grows only where soil was honestly kept and marks good custody. A farm fails because one operator cannot watch fifty escrows at once, and one neglected watch poisons every fake under its care; honest custodians earn the anchor one season at a time.
